items.prompt: A procurement assistant has twenty available tools, but its current workflow only searches suppliers, retrieves one contract, and summarizes it. Tool descriptions consume much of the initial context. Which configuration is the best first release?
constraints: Supplier search, contract retrieval, and summarization are the high-use path.
Rare governed capabilities must remain available without occupying the initial context.

options.text: Expose all twenty tools at startup so Claude can choose among every procurement capability without a discovery step.
Keep the three precise read tools available for this workflow and defer rare governed tools to an explicit discovery path.
Remove every tool except a text generator and have procurement staff perform supplier and contract lookups outside the assistant.
Expose only one universal procurement tool with optional parameters so the model sees fewer names while retaining every operation.

feedback.Reason: The common workflow needs precise schemas immediately; rare capabilities can be discovered when their governed use is actually selected. This reduces context and selection ambiguity without deleting valid behavior.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: A curated initial inventory keeps high-use tool contracts visible while tool search or another controlled discovery mechanism loads detailed rare capabilities only when relevant.
Details.scenarioApplication: The assistant can search suppliers, retrieve the selected contract, and summarize it directly; an approved discovery path handles uncommon export or mutation workflows.
Details.errorCorrection: Treat tool descriptions as part of the context budget and capability boundary rather than exposing every operation merely because it exists.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Discovery adds one step for rare requests, but it preserves the long tail while reducing initial context pressure and wrong-tool selection.
Details.transfer: For a large tool catalog, measure use and selection quality, keep the narrow high-use surface eager, and discover governed long-tail tools on demand.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Loading all definitions recreates the context bloat and leaves similar or rare capabilities competing with the three required tools.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Removing capabilities turns a context problem into an unsupported manual process and loses legitimate procurement workflows.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: A universal schema hides distinct contracts behind optional parameters and can increase invalid combinations and selection errors.

items.prompt: A finance assistant has four tools named fetch_invoice, search_invoice, lookup_invoice, and retrieve_invoice. They accept different filters, overlap in purpose, and the assistant often selects a contract that cannot satisfy the request. What should be diagnosed first?
constraints: Each exposed capability should have one distinct operation and a predictable filter contract.
The selection errors occur among overlapping tools rather than from a missing finance data source.

options.text: Add aliases and examples for all four tools so Claude has more wording clues while preserving the overlapping contracts.
Call all four tools for each request, compare their results, and let Claude choose the most complete invoice record.
Consolidate the overlapping surface into canonical identifier and search tools with distinct names, filters, and contract tests.
Expose the underlying database for arbitrary queries so Claude can bypass the ambiguous tool descriptions.

feedback.Reason: The defect is capability ambiguity: overlapping names and incompatible filters make a valid request map to the wrong contract. Canonical tools reduce choices and make parameters testable.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Distinct tool schemas and descriptions give each operation a clear selection boundary; typed validation rejects unsupported filters before execution.
Details.scenarioApplication: Keep one exact invoice lookup and one filtered search, document their identifier and filter semantics, and evaluate selection and parameter validity on representative requests.
Details.errorCorrection: Diagnose overlapping capability surfaces before adding prompt prose, retries, or unrestricted database access.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Consolidation may require callers to migrate and can remove convenient aliases, but it lowers wrong-tool calls and protects the typed authorization boundary.
Details.transfer: When similar tools cause selection errors, reduce the canonical surface and test operation and parameter contracts instead of increasing choice.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: More aliases preserve four competing contracts and add wording without removing the ambiguity that caused the wrong selection.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Calling every tool multiplies latency and permissions and still leaves the model to reconcile incompatible filters.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Arbitrary database access bypasses typed and authorized capability boundaries and makes the selection problem less observable.

items.prompt: A claims assistant receives every matching policy record, sometimes 10,000 rows, even when the user asks about one claim. The model then misses the relevant clause. Which tool boundary should replace that response shape?
constraints: The active context needs bounded relevant results.
The full result set must remain queryable through explicit continuation and detail paths.

options.text: Return the complete result set in pages but place the first page in context and ask Claude to summarize before requesting more pages.
Return a fixed first page of ten rows and rely on the model to continue only when it recognizes that the target claim is absent.
Return a filtered count plus a human-operated search link, leaving the assistant unable to retrieve an exact clause during the normal path.
Require filters and pagination, return concise matches with a continuation token, and expose a bounded detail lookup by record ID.

feedback.Reason: The tool should constrain intermediate context without hiding valid evidence. Pagination and detail lookup preserve access to the full set while making the common claim query focused.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Programmatic filtering and pagination process results before model exposure; a continuation token and record-ID lookup provide deliberate expansion when the user needs it.
Details.scenarioApplication: Filter by claim and active policy version, return a small ranked page, and let Claude request the next page or exact clause instead of receiving 10,000 rows.
Details.errorCorrection: Put result shaping at the tool boundary and make truncation or continuation explicit; do not rely on the model to recover from an oversized or silently incomplete response.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The design may require another tool call for a broad question, but it protects attention and makes completeness an observable choice.
Details.transfer: For large intermediate results, process and bound them before model context while preserving an explicit path to inspect the authoritative source.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Pagination alone still returns broad pages and leaves selection to the model; without claim-specific filters and a record-level detail contract, the relevant clause can remain buried and page requests become model-driven.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Silent truncation can hide the relevant clause and gives no reliable way to tell whether the first page was complete.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: A count alone removes the evidence needed for the answer and turns an addressable tool problem into unnecessary manual work.

items.prompt: A building-permit platform serves three municipalities through one catalog of 80 tools. Each municipality authorizes a different subset; three core reads dominate, while regional forms and exports are rare. Which TWO configuration decisions preserve capability and authorization? Select TWO.
constraints: Tool visibility must follow the validated requesting tenant and user.
High-use authorized reads should be immediate, while rare governed capabilities remain discoverable.

options.text: Load all 80 definitions for every municipality so the model can discover regional differences from the catalog.
Keep the authorized high-use reads eager and defer rare regional tools so ordinary requests retain their precise contracts without the full catalog.
Delete rare regional tools from the catalog because their low frequency makes their maintenance cost disproportionate.
Show every tool to the model but rely on municipality names in the prompt to prevent cross-tenant calls.
Scope discovery results by validated tenant and user, and recheck the current operation scope at invocation before executing a discovered regional form or export.

feedback.Reason: The common capability surface can be curated per tenant, but rare tools should remain available through controlled discovery. Discovery and execution both need tenant-aware authorization; visibility alone is insufficient.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Tenant and user identity scope the catalog and discovery results, while the server rechecks current permission at invocation before executing a tool.
Details.scenarioApplication: Expose the municipality's three core reads, discover regional forms and exports only for that tenant, and reject a stale or cross-tenant request at the server boundary.
Details.errorCorrection: Separate context optimization from authorization: defer capabilities by use, but never let a model-visible catalog grant access.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Tenant-scoped discovery adds filtering and invocation checks, yet it retains rare business behavior without exposing unauthorized schemas or actions.
Details.transfer: In multi-tenant catalogs, curate the eager set by validated access and usage, then enforce the same scope again at execution.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: A global eager catalog consumes context and exposes irrelevant or unauthorized capability descriptions to every municipality.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Frequency alone is not a reason to delete valid regional behavior; discovery can preserve it without eager context cost.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Prompt wording is not an authorization boundary and can be bypassed by a manipulated or stale request.

omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.b: Without an eager authorized core, the common path is either bloated with irrelevant tools or lacks its precise read contracts.
omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.e: Without tenant-scoped discovery and an invocation recheck, rare tools can leak across municipalities or execute after permissions change.

items.prompt: A reporting tool exposes eighteen optional filters, four mutually exclusive output modes, and nullable identifiers. Malformed combinations cause retries, although this workflow needs only ID lookup and date-bounded search. Which redesign is best?
constraints: The visible workflow needs two narrow operations.
Invalid filter and output combinations should be unrepresentable or rejected before execution.

options.text: Keep one universal tool with examples for common combinations, validate only after a service error, and let the model retry with a revised optional-field set.
Hide the four output modes in prose while retaining their union schema, then accept the model's selected mode when the backend can coerce it.
Split the surface into typed identifier-lookup and date-bounded-search tools with required fields, and remove unused modes from this workflow.
Accept every parameter combination and normalize incompatible filters in a gateway after the reporting service rejects the request.

feedback.Reason: A union-shaped tool makes the model choose among combinations the workflow does not need. Two purpose-specific schemas make required fields and invalid modes explicit before execution.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Typed narrow tools reduce the model-visible action space and allow application validation to reject unsupported combinations before an expensive or failing call.
Details.scenarioApplication: Use an ID lookup for exact records and a date-bounded search for ranges, with required identifiers or dates and clear result contracts.
Details.errorCorrection: Simplify the canonical capability boundary around actual operations instead of compensating for a broad schema with more prose or retries.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Some future modes need a separate tool or contract, but the current workflow gains predictable calls and fewer retry loops.
Details.transfer: When a tool union creates invalid combinations, split by operation and validate the narrow contract before execution.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Examples can guide selection but do not make incompatible optional fields impossible and leave retries as the error control.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Hiding modes while preserving the union still exposes the same parameter ambiguity and makes the schema disagree with the intended capability.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Normalizing after a service error spends a call and treats a preventable contract defect as runtime recovery.

items.prompt: A security audit asks for counts by actor and day across 100,000 event records, plus a few event IDs for drill-down. The model needs the aggregate, not every raw row. Which tool design is appropriate?
constraints: The aggregate must be complete and arithmetically correct.
Operators still need a bounded path to inspect representative source events.

options.text: Aggregate and filter in the service or programmatic tool, expose the summary and representative event IDs, and provide a separate bounded detail call.
Return the 100,000 events to a programmatic model tool, ask Claude to group them, and let the model choose drill-down IDs from its truncated context.
Use a statistically selected event sample to estimate actor/day counts, and give operators no deterministic way to inspect the excluded rows.
Expose a free-form database query and ask Claude to summarize whichever rows fit the context, without an explicit aggregate or scope contract.

feedback.Reason: The service can compute a complete aggregate without spending model context on every row, while IDs preserve an evidence path for drill-down.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Programmatic filtering and aggregation handle arithmetic and membership; the model receives a compact result and can request a deliberately bounded detail view.
Details.scenarioApplication: Filter by audit scope, group by actor and day, return counts with selected event IDs and time ranges, and fetch details only for requested IDs.
Details.errorCorrection: Process large intermediate results before exposing them to Claude; preserve source addresses instead of using context size as an implicit sampling rule.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A separate detail call adds interaction for forensic questions, but it protects aggregate correctness and avoids a massive token and latency cost.
Details.transfer: For analytics over large records, keep computation and completeness in the structured service and expose compact, auditable evidence handles.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Raw rows pollute context and make completeness and arithmetic depend on the model receiving every event.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: A random sample cannot answer a complete count and offers no path to verify a disputed event.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Free-form context-limited queries make result membership implicit and can expose more data than the audit question requires.

items.prompt:
A small internal assistant has five tools: search, fetch, update, notify, and close. All five are used by every request path, their typed definitions total 1% of context, and the server can enforce authorization at invocation.

Which tool-surface strategy is proportionate to this small, universal inventory?
constraints: All five typed tools are used on every request and consume only 1% of context.
A second discovery round adds 400 ms and no rare capability needs deferral.
Server-side authorization at invocation must remain in force.

options.text: Use a discovery mechanism first and defer every tool because eager capability exposure is always harmful.
Eagerly load the five governed typed tools and retain invocation authorization; defer discovery until the inventory changes.
Expose only search and fetch initially, then discover update, notify, and close for each route that needs them.
Flatten the five definitions into prose and let the model choose calls without typed schemas, using the server only for transport.

feedback.Reason: The context and latency evidence reverses the large-inventory default: eager core plus deferred tail has no tail to defer here.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends loading the most critical tools while deferring others for discovery when the tool inventory is large. The scenario's mechanism is governed by this decisive constraint: The inventory is small, stable, and universally needed, so eager exposure is preferable to deferred discovery.
Details.scenarioApplication: Load all five governed tool definitions in the initial request, retain server-side authorization and typed schemas, and reserve discovery for a future inventory change.
Details.errorCorrection: The definitions consume negligible context and every request needs them, so discovery adds avoidable latency and complexity.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the inventory grows or rare tools make up most definitions, restore a critical eager set and governed deferred discovery.
Details.transfer: Route each information need through the smallest governed interface that matches its evidence shape, and preserve explicit authorization, freshness, and unavailable states when the evidence cannot support a claim.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: The definitions consume negligible context and every request needs them, so discovery adds avoidable latency and complexity.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: This creates the measured second-round latency even though all five tools are universal and already fit comfortably in context.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Replacing typed definitions removes contract clarity and does not improve authorization; invocation enforcement must remain independent of prompt exposure.

items.prompt:
After a catalog release adds twelve tools, wrong-tool selection rises from 0.5% to 4.2% while transport p95 stays unchanged. Two tools have similar names but different tenant filters, and traces record only the final answer, not the selected tool or inventory version.

Which catalog repair makes tool selection observable and less ambiguous?
constraints: Wrong-tool selection rose from 0.5% to 4.2% after twelve tools were added, while transport p95 stayed stable.
Two tools have similar names but different tenant filters.
The application can version the inventory and trace tool, parameters, authorization, and outcome.

options.text: Keep all tools visible and tune model temperature because the transport p95 metric is healthy.
Merge the similar tools behind one broad tool with an optional tenant filter so the model has fewer names to choose from.
Split overlapping tools with required filters, version the inventory, and trace selection, authorization, parameters, and outcomes.
Add aliases and longer descriptions to the existing catalog, but keep only final-answer logging because selection traces add overhead.

feedback.Reason: The decision addresses both capability bloat and the evidence needed to determine whether the repair works.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic notes that tools with similar names can lead to wrong tool selection and incorrect parameters. The scenario's mechanism is governed by this decisive constraint: The capability surface needs schema clarity and observable selection outcomes; latency alone cannot identify or repair the new tool-choice failure.
Details.scenarioApplication: Split overlapping capabilities into canonical tools with distinct required filters, version the inventory, and trace the selected tool, parameters, authorization, and result before expanding the catalog.
Details.errorCorrection: The defect is wrong selection and parameters, not transport latency; extra visibility and randomness can increase the ambiguity.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If traces show the errors come from a single malformed backend response rather than selection, repair that contract and keep the tool surface unchanged.
Details.transfer: Route each information need through the smallest governed interface that matches its evidence shape, and preserve explicit authorization, freshness, and unavailable states when the evidence cannot support a claim.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: The defect is wrong selection and parameters, not transport latency; extra visibility and randomness can increase ambiguity.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: An optional filter hides a material tenant distinction and can make an incorrect scope look valid instead of requiring the correct typed field.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Descriptions may help, but without canonical required fields, versioning, and selection traces the observed choice and parameter failure cannot be diagnosed.
